problem:
The acceleration $a$ at time $t$ of a particle $P$ moving in the $xy$-plane is given by

$$
a(t)=⟨3{t}^{2},t+\frac{1}{2}⟩.
$$

Given that the particle has velocity $v=⟨1,-1⟩$ when $t=1,$ calculate the velocity vector of $P$ at time $t=2.$

activity_context.topic_title: Finding Velocity Vectors in Two Dimensions Using Integration

feedback.problem:
The acceleration $a$ at time $t$ of a particle $P$ moving in the $xy$-plane is given by

$$
a(t)=⟨\frac{1}{\sqrt{{t}^{3}}},t⟩,\,t\in (0,\infty ).
$$

Given that the particle has velocity $v=⟨1,-1⟩$ when $t=1,$ calculate the velocity vector of $P$ at time $t=4.$
feedback.worked_solution:
To compute the velocity vector, we need to integrate the acceleration vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int ⟨\frac{1}{\sqrt{{t}^{3}}},t⟩\text{d}t \\  & =⟨\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{{t}^{3}}}\,\text{d}t,\int t\,\text{d}t⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{2}{\sqrt{t}}+{C}_{1},\frac{{t}^{2}}{2}+{C}_{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can solve for the constants of integration using the fact that $v(1)=⟨1,-1⟩.$ Substituting $t=1,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}v(1) & =⟨-\frac{2}{\sqrt{1}}+{C}_{1},\frac{{1}^{2}}{2}+{C}_{2}⟩ \\ ⟨1,-1⟩ & =⟨-2+{C}_{1},\frac{1}{2}+{C}_{2}⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

so we must have ${C}_{1}=3$ and ${C}_{2}=-\frac{3}{2}.$ Therefore, the velocity is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =⟨-\frac{2}{\sqrt{t}}+3,\frac{{t}^{2}}{2}-\frac{3}{2}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the velocity at time $t=4$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}v(4) & =⟨-\frac{2}{\sqrt{4}}+3,\frac{{4}^{2}}{2}-\frac{3}{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\frac{13}{2}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
